#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=rate_shift_type
#   --mail-type=END,FAIL
#   --mail-user=b.kopperud@lmu.de
#   --mem-per-cpu=4GB
#   --output=logs/rate_shift_type.log
#   --error=logs/rate_shift_type.err
#   --qos=low_prio_res
#   --ntasks=1
#   --nodes=1
#   --cpus-per-task=100
#   --partition=krypton

#flux: --job-name=rate_shift_type
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 100

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem-per-cpu=4GB
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm options: --qos=low_prio_res and --partition=krypton
# Flux QoS/queue/partition selection are site-specific; no portable equivalents.
# Performance implication: job may run with different limits/priority or on different hardware (or be rejected by policy).

# Omitted Slurm options: --mail-type and --mail-user
# Flux does not provide a universal, built-in email notification directive in batch scripts.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but you will not receive automatic job emails.

# Output/error paths are set explicitly in Slurm; Flux output directives are not used here.
# Performance implication: none, but logs will go to Flux defaults unless redirected in commands.

module load R/4.3.2 gnu openblas

export R_HOME="/opt/cres/lib/hpc/gcc7/R/4.2.3/lib64/R"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/opt/cres/lib/hpc/gcc7/R/4.2.3/lib64/R/lib"

# SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK is not set under Flux; use the allocated cores-per-task (100).
julia --threads 100 scripts/06_rate_shift_type_inference.jl > logs/rate_shift_type_inference.txt

reasons: The original Slurm job requested memory per CPU (`--mem-per-cpu=4GB`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.

The original Slurm job specified a partition and QoS (`--partition=krypton`, `--qos=low_prio_res`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/QoS selection; on sites where these affect eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.
